sentences.text: Janassa species possessed a body plan very similar to modern rays, despite sharing no evolutionary kinship with them.
This animal lived for an immense span of time, from 346.7 to 254.14 million years ago.
The genus Janassa was first described by Schlotheim in 1820.
Fossils are known from teeth and poorly preserved body remains found in the Kupferschiefer of Germany and the Marl Slate of England.
The teeth suggest the animal crushed and ate shellfish like brachiopods.
Based on tooth structure, Janassa is thought to have fed on shelled animals by crushing them.
Janassa belongs to the class Chondrichthyes, the order Petalodontiformes, and the family Janassidae.
Five species are recognized within the genus, including the type species J. bituminosa.
Janassa fossils date from the Lower Carboniferous to the Lopingian periods.
